Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.
7:Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.
13:Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.
21:A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

---
figure: FIG. 1
numerals: [10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 66]
---


View: front elevation of the clamp closed around a pipe, along the pipe axis. Patent line drawing, black line work on white, no shading or color. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

Geometry to draw:

- A pipe drawn as one plain circle at the center of the drawing area, occupying roughly the middle third of its width, its interior empty.
- Around that circle, an annular frame body drawn as an outer boundary and an inner boundary, concentric with the pipe circle and spaced outward from it, so a band of frame material surrounds the pipe. It is divided into two substantially semicircular halves by radial breaks at the left and at the right, the upper half and the lower half drawn as separate solids meeting at those breaks.
- At the left break, a hinge drawn as a small circle straddling the two halves, with a short pair of straight lines joining it to each half, so the halves are visibly pivoted together there.
- At the right break, a latch drawn as a compact rectangular body attached across the two halves and overlapping both, with a straight lever arm extending outward and downward to the right.
- Three carriage blocks at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, none of them at either break. - Between the inner end of each carriage block and the pipe circle, a small block whose inner edge is a concave arc meeting the pipe circle, so that this small block, and not the carriage block, contacts the pipe.
- A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular pad on the outer boundary of the annular frame body at the upper right, projecting radially outward and joined to it.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.
